author: Han Li
description:
US lawmakers have been demanding answers about potential national security risks and White House oversight of advanced chip exports to China following revelations that former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang was in a relationship with a businesswoman suspected of working for Chinese intelligence.
Three Republican House committee chairmen and Senate Banking Committee chairman Tim Scott separately sent letters Thursday seeking testimony from Huang.
“As reports continue to come to light...
title: US Congress widens Nvidia probe, seeking testimony from Jensen Huang and Trump officials

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
When G7 leaders gathered at the French resort of Evian-les-Bains in June, Donald Trump arrived late but wasted no time in grabbing the spotlight. With a cheeky declaration, “I am the boss”, the US president drew a ripple of awkward laughter from around the table.
Months earlier, in his September 2025 address to the UN General Assembly, he told the gathering that “your countries are going to hell”. His lengthy speech blended boasts about his own record with sharp criticism of allies’ policies,...
title: Midterm losses could give Trump a quest to emerge from Apec summit as a winner

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
Air travel across the United States came to a halt on Friday afternoon after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered all flights grounded because of a communications breakdown at the regional centres that manage the country’s air traffic.
Citing “extraordinary circumstances” and “reasons of safety”, the FAA said in a notice that the halt would stay in place until at least 11pm Eastern time on Friday.
In a social media post, the agency described the problem as a temporary...
title: All US flights grounded due to communication issues: homeland security head

author: Zhou Xiaoming
description:
The European Commission is moving to shield its industrial machinery and chemical sectors from Chinese imports, and is weighing a “kill switch” mechanism.
Together with Washington, Brussels has settled into a familiar narrative: a record trade deficit with China is framed as proof of its “overcapacity” and attributed to state subsidies that allegedly tilt the global playing field.
For European Union audiences frustrated by stagnant domestic manufacturing, this argument sounds intuitive. Held up...
title: EU’s fixation on Chinese subsidies masks its own structural stagnation

author: Nayan Seth,Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Friday blamed the Commerce Department, led by Howard Lutnick, for delaying the blacklisting of Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of diverting advanced AI chips to China, days before US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are expected to meet in Shenzhen.
Bessent spoke a day after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive following reports that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based...
title: Bessent blames US Commerce Department for not restricting Nvidia chip exports to China

author: Nayan Seth
description:
The United States and China held the inaugural meeting of their bilateral Board of Trade on Friday, just days before US President Donald Trump is set to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.
“Today, the Office of the US Trade Representative, alongside the @USTreasury, held the first official US-China Board of Trade meeting with our Chinese counterparts,” the US Trade Representative (USTR) said on social media.
“The Trump Administration looks forward to continuing our engagement with China...
title: US-China Board of Trade holds first meeting days before Trump-Xi summit

author: Dewey Sim,Khushboo Razdan,Nayan Seth
description:
US President Donald Trump will press Southeast Asian economies to join Pax Silica, his campaign to China-proof AI and chip supply chains, when he attends the Asean summit in Manila next week.
According to people familiar with the matter, artificial intelligence and critical minerals will top his agenda at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations gathering, his first trip abroad since his party’s bruising midterm defeats.
In particular, he is expected to urge regional leaders to sign up for AI...
title: Trump to press Southeast Asia nations to join Pax Silica at Asean summit in Manila

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
China and the United States have a shared interest in preventing artificial intelligence (AI) from being misused, but differing views over what constitutes a serious safety incident could complicate efforts to build a bilateral communication mechanism, according to analysts.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday that Washington and Beijing should cooperate on AI risks while harbouring no illusions about their differences.
He noted the two governments had established a new dialogue...
title: US-China AI safety talks face hurdle over how to define ‘serious’ incidents: analysts

author: Shi Huang
description:
In early November, a low-resolution photo of an internal meeting circulated on China’s social networks, accompanied by a caption with only one sentence: “It is said that he is a top-tier introduced talent at the 10,000-tonne level.”
The main person in the photo is leading biologist Zhao Yingming, who was the Louis Block Professor in the Ben May Department for Cancer Research at the University of Chicago. He has just joined Zhejiang University in Hangzhou, according to sources.
Zhejiang...
title: ‘10,000-tonne level talent’ biologist Zhao Yingming leaves Chicago for Hangzhou

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Algeria’s military has released footage showing what appears to be the export variant of China’s YJ-12 supersonic anti-ship missile being test-fired along the country’s Mediterranean coast, offering a rare glimpse of an advanced Chinese weapon in service with one of Beijing’s African military customers.
The weapon was launched from a mobile coastal-defence system near the western Algerian city of Oran on Tuesday, striking a target at sea during the country’s Mediterranean Falcon 2026 military...
title: Algeria test-fires apparent Chinese YJ-12 supersonic missile in Mediterranean drill

author: William Zheng
description:
Reports that two Chinese nationals were convicted in Mongolia for making unauthorised impressions of a celebrated 2,000-year-old Han dynasty cliff inscription have ignited discussion and concern over protecting historic sites.
The online uproar emerged this week as Chinese internet users and experts in Inner Mongolia noted that the landmark site had been subjected to illegal tampering since its rediscovery was made known nearly a decade ago.
The case stems from an incident in November last year...
title: How a bad impression put a celebrated 2,000-year-old Han cliff inscription at risk

author: Dannie Peng
description:
A Chinese pianist ordered to secure research funding to save his university job has died, while a note that he left exposing alleged malpractices at the institution was posthumously posted online by one of his students – with his family’s consent.
The note was penned by Bai Baoguo. Born in 1972, Bai was an associate professor at the Yan’an University’s Luxun Academy of Fine Arts in Shaanxi province. He died on October 20.
Two weeks later, on November 3, a six-page note circulated on the Chinese...
title: No research fund, no teaching job: late Chinese pianist’s note published by student

author: SCMP
description:
We have selected seven stories from this week’s news across Hong Kong, mainland China, the wider Asia region and beyond that resonated with our readers and shed light on topical issues. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid affairs scandal
Jensen Huang has resigned as president, chief executive officer and board member of the AI chip giant Nvidia with immediate effect, the firm announced on Thursday, amid media...
title: Jensen Huang quits Nvidia; non-invasive treatment for kidney tumours: SCMP’s 7 highlights

author: Seong Hyeon Choi,Zhang Tong
description:
We were weeks into a three-month assignment reporting from the SCMP bureau in Washington when we heard a shooting just around the corner from our apartment building.
From our flat, we often hear trucks going past and loud noise from the ventilation system several storeys below.
But as we got ready for work at 8am on Thursday we heard something unusual – “bang, bang, bang”. It was gunfire, and it sounded like it was right outside our apartment.
Soon after, we heard fire alarms, police sirens and...
title: Shooting close to home: reporter’s view of a grim reality in the US capital
